definitions.explanation: Without any delay. A formal and emphatic way to say immediately, often used in demands, orders, or urgent situations.

examples.japanese: {即刻|そっこく}{出|で}て{行|い}け。
{問題|もんだい}が{発覚|はっかく}し、{即刻|そっこく}{対応|たいおう}が{求|もと}められた。
examples.english: The problem was discovered and an immediate response was demanded.

examples.japanese: {不正|ふせい}が{明|あき}らかになった{社員|しゃいん}は{即刻|そっこく}{解雇|かいこ}された。
examples.english: The employee whose misconduct was revealed was fired on the spot.

notes: More formal and forceful than すぐ or すぐに. Often appears in commands, demands, and official actions such as {即刻|そっこく}{解雇|かいこ} (immediate dismissal), {即刻|そっこく}{中止|ちゅうし} (immediate halt), and {即刻|そっこく}{退去|たいきょ} (immediate evacuation). Similar to {直|ただ}ちに but carries a stronger sense of urgency and is more commonly used in confrontational or authoritative contexts.
